evals.name: inactivity-timer
evals.prompt: Write a Go worker loop with a five-second inactivity timeout that reports inactivity and keeps waiting. Target Go 1.23 timer semantics. Support cancellation.

assertions.text: Resets the inactivity deadline on activity and after reporting inactivity; does not substitute a periodic ticker.
Avoids repeated timer allocation in the hot loop and permits cancellation and closed-input termination.
Does not use an unconditional stale-channel drain under Go 1.23 timer semantics.

evals.name: consumer-stops-early
evals.prompt: A Go consumer has enough results and wants to close the producer channel to stop production. Design termination and completion ownership.

assertions.text: Uses a stop signal instead of racing channel close with producer sends.
Makes blocked production interruptible and provides a way to observe producer completion.
Assigns channel closure to an owner that knows all sends have ended.

evals.name: waitgroup-registration
evals.prompt: Review Go code that calls wg.Add(1) inside each goroutine, defers wg.Done(), and calls wg.Wait() after the spawn loop. Fix it for Go 1.24.

assertions.text: Registers work before spawning, either individually or as a known batch.
Explains why Wait can otherwise observe zero and return early.
Balances completion and does not use WaitGroup.Go on Go 1.24.

evals.name: pipeline-directions
evals.prompt: Implement a cancellable Go generator and doubling stage. Input may stay open and idle; the consumer may stop early. Explain completion.

assertions.text: Exposes directional channel APIs appropriate to each caller.
Makes both input receive and output send cancellable.
Closes output after sends finish and lets the owner observe completion.

evals.name: bounded-queue
evals.prompt: Design the channel capacity for a Go dispatcher feeding workers. Bursts are possible but memory must stay bounded.

assertions.text: Ties capacity to handoff, burst, or measured workload needs rather than an arbitrary large number.
Defines backpressure or rejection when capacity is exhausted.
Bounds queued and active work and describes shutdown.

evals.name: handoff-aliases
evals.prompt: A Go producer sends Task values containing Payload []byte to workers, then immediately reuses the payload buffer. Review and fix ownership.

assertions.text: Identifies that copying Task does not copy the byte storage.
Uses sufficient copying, exclusive transfer, or synchronization to prevent concurrent mutation.
Does not claim pointers are inherently unsafe or value channels inherently safe.

evals.name: bounded-fetches
evals.prompt: Implement concurrent Go fetching of 50 URLs, at most ten active, canceling remaining work on the first error and waiting for started work.

assertions.text: Bounds active fetches and propagates cancellation to HTTP work.
Reports the failure and joins started work before returning.
Uses errgroup or a correct equivalent; does not claim SetLimit admission itself is context-cancellable.

evals.name: map-invariants
evals.prompt: Choose synchronization for a Go cache with frequent overlapping writes and a cross-key invariant. Reads and writes are equally frequent.

assertions.text: Protects the cross-key invariant with coordinated locking or equivalent ownership.
Does not assume sync.Map operations provide a multi-key transaction.
Avoids unconditional speed claims about Mutex, RWMutex, and sync.Map.

evals.name: pool-alias-lifetime
evals.prompt: Review a Go encoder that takes a bytes.Buffer from sync.Pool, returns buf.Bytes(), and defers putting the buffer back. Include clean-state requirements.

assertions.text: Identifies returned bytes alias pooled storage that may be reused.
Copies output or transfers ownership without returning the still-aliased buffer.
Establishes clean buffer state and does not treat the pool as persistent storage.

evals.name: background-panic-policy
evals.prompt: Design asynchronous notifications in a Go HTTP service returning 202. Address panics, overload, errors, and shutdown.

assertions.text: Bounds work and gives it service-level completion and shutdown ownership.
Defines whether panic recovery is a deliberate isolation boundary and reports failures if recovering.
Does not silently recover or claim HTTP handler recovery catches a child goroutine panic.

evals.name: singleflight-contexts
evals.prompt: Deduplicate simultaneous Go profile lookups. Each caller can cancel independently; the shared lookup should survive one waiter leaving but have a bounded lifetime.

assertions.text: Uses singleflight or equivalent per-key in-flight suppression with a separate bounded lookup lifetime.
Allows waiters to stop waiting independently.
Does not claim DoChan waiter cancellation cancels shared work or singleflight caches completed results.

evals.name: sequential-transform
evals.prompt: In Go 1.23, should a small in-memory filter/map of users to emails use a goroutine pipeline? Explain the choice.

assertions.text: Chooses a loop or iterator for this small sequential transform.
Explains when overlap or sufficient parallel work could justify goroutines.
Does not claim all CPU-bound work is unsuitable for concurrency.

evals.name: request-propagation
evals.prompt: Write a Go order handler that queries a database and calls a payment status API. Both must respect request cancellation.

assertions.text: Propagates r.Context() or derived children through both operations.
Uses context-aware SQL and HTTP APIs.
Keeps the HTTP context alive through body consumption and closes owned bodies.

evals.name: retry-scope
evals.prompt: Write a Go HTTP retry function with three attempts, five seconds per attempt, caller cancellation, and a returned byte slice.

assertions.text: Derives each attempt from the caller and releases its cancel function and response body before the next attempt.
Consumes the body before canceling its request context.
Stops on caller cancellation, including during backoff.

evals.name: typed-metadata
evals.prompt: Write Go middleware and a cross-package accessor for a tenant ID already authenticated by earlier middleware.

assertions.text: Uses a package-private comparable key type with a typed accessor.
Handles missing metadata without panic.
Does not treat an arbitrary client header as authenticated identity.

evals.name: draining-worker
evals.prompt: Design Go Worker Start and Stop methods. Stop must reject new jobs, finish the current job, and report completion.

assertions.text: Separates admission stop from aborting current work.
Provides observable completion rather than only a cancel call.
Keeps per-call and owned worker lifetimes explicit without mechanically forbidding all lifetime-owning structs.

evals.name: detached-audit
evals.prompt: A Go 1.21 payment handler must asynchronously deliver an audit event with trace metadata even if the client disconnects. Delivery must survive process restart.

assertions.text: Explains that WithoutCancel preserves values but removes cancellation and deadline.
Uses durable delivery such as an outbox or queue for restart survival rather than promising a goroutine is durable.
Bounds and owns any in-process detached work.

evals.name: nested-budgets
evals.prompt: A Go operation has a ten-second total timeout. Cache gets two seconds, then database must get its full eight seconds even if cache used two seconds plus overhead. Implement the budget.

assertions.text: Identifies the incompatible full-duration guarantee under the total deadline.
Derives operation timeouts from the parent and respects its remaining budget.
Releases owned cancel functions without detaching to bypass the total deadline.

evals.name: incremental-context
evals.prompt: Plan incremental context propagation in Go from main through request handlers and services to database calls. Some intermediate APIs do not accept context yet.

assertions.text: Uses TODO only as an explicit temporary gap and roots Background at an owned entry point.
Uses real request contexts where available rather than substituting placeholders.
Shows a path to remove gaps and never passes nil context.

evals.name: transaction-context
evals.prompt: Review database/sql code that accepts ctx, calls db.Begin(), then tx.ExecContext(ctx, ...), then tx.Commit(). Fix context propagation.

assertions.text: Uses BeginTx(ctx, nil) or appropriate options.
Keeps ctx on transaction operations and handles rollback/error ownership.
Does not invent sql.Tx.CommitContext or RollbackContext.

evals.name: value-boundaries
evals.prompt: Design ProcessOrder in Go with a database, base logger, authenticated identity, trace ID, and order details.

assertions.text: Keeps database and order arguments explicit rather than hiding them in context.
Uses context metadata for suitable request-scoped identity and tracing.
Distinguishes a base logger dependency from a request-enriched logger convention.

evals.name: afterfunc-coordination
evals.prompt: In Go 1.21 register cancellation cleanup with AfterFunc while ordinary completion also releases the same resource. The release is not safe to call twice or concurrently.

assertions.text: Coordinates exactly-once release and resource use rather than racing two cleanups.
Explains that stopping AfterFunc does not join a callback already running.
Handles ordinary completion even if context never cancels.

evals.name: blocked-admission
evals.prompt: Review a Go function using errgroup.WithContext and SetLimit(1). The first task ignores context and blocks forever; the producer is blocked submitting the second task. Will canceling ctx release Go or Wait?

assertions.text: Explains neither admission nor Wait is forced to return by cancellation.
Addresses the noncooperative dependency and context-aware admission where required.
Does not fix bounded execution by spawning an unbounded number of admission goroutines.

evals.name: group-context-after-wait
evals.prompt: A Go function successfully waits for errgroup.WithContext then uses the derived context for a final database write. Review it.

assertions.text: Identifies that the group context is canceled when Wait returns, even on success.
Uses a suitable still-live parent or separately owned context for post-group work.
Preserves the caller deadline rather than switching blindly to Background.

evals.name: select-work-evaluation
evals.prompt: Review Go code: select { case out <- expensive(ctx): case <-ctx.Done(): return }. Does it skip expensive when canceled? Does select prioritize cancellation?

assertions.text: Explains send operands are evaluated before selection.
Explains ready cancellation has no select priority.
Gives expensive work a cancellation contract and states the limits of preliminary checks.
